full_goal_lean_formula:
(∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G] (xs : List G),
  xs.length = 2 * Fintype.card G - 1 →
  ∃ ys : List G, ys.Sublist xs ∧ ys.length = Fintype.card G ∧ ys.prod = 1)

claims.exact_quantified_statement: For every finite group G of order n and every list xs of length 2n-1, there is an increasing-index sublist ys of length n whose product, in that order, is 1.
assumptions: G is a finite group; n is its cardinality.
The input list has exactly 2n-1 entries.
claims.scope_detail: The all-groups target has neither been proved nor refuted in this round.
claims.prior_art_relation: Dimitrov 2004 proves the ordered p-group cases. Reorderable results and one-short dihedral words do not resolve this statement.

claims.exact_quantified_statement: For every group G, elements u,v,z with u*u=v*v=z and z commuting with u and v, every integer h>=0, and every list xs of length 2h+1 with all entries in {u,v}, there exists ys.Sublist xs with length 2h and ordered product z^h.
claims.scope_detail: An alphabet-restricted cancellation lemma. If z^h=1 it rules out certain counterexample templates; it gives no universal ordered EGZ theorem.
claims.prior_art_relation: Elementary adjacent-pair cancellation; no originality claim.

claims.exact_quantified_statement: In Dic_3=<r,s | r^6=1, s^2=r^3, s*r*s^(-1)=r^(-1)> of order 12, the list (s,r,s^(-1),r^(-1)) has identity products on sublists (1,3) and (2,4), but its increasing-index union product equals r^4 != 1.
assumptions: The specified Dic_3 group and the specified four-term list.
claims.scope_detail: Refutes a proposed interleaved-block lifting step, not Olson ordered EGZ.
claims.prior_art_relation: Standard noncommutativity obstruction, made explicit in a non-p-group; no originality claim.

claims.exact_quantified_statement: For every j>=0, (r-1)^(2^j)=r^(2^j)-1 != 0 in F_2[Dic_3], where r has order 6; also (s-1)^(3^j)=s^(3^j)-1 != 0 in F_3[Dic_3], where s has order 4. In either field the augmentation ideal is not nilpotent.
assumptions: G is Dic_3 with r of order 6 and s of order 4.
The respective coefficient fields are F_2 and F_3.
claims.scope_detail: An obstruction to assuming augmentation-ideal nilpotence beyond p-groups, not an obstruction to the conjecture itself.
claims.prior_art_relation: Standard modular group-algebra fact; the familiar cyclic-subalgebra argument is reproduced only to expose the method limitation.

claims.exact_quantified_statement: For each concrete table and sequence in instances below, the table is a group of the given order n, the list has length 2n-1, and the set of all increasing n-index tuples giving ordered product 1 has cardinality exactly identity_subset_count.
assumptions: Only the three concrete tables and explicit lists in instances; no generalization to other lists is made.
claims.scope_detail: Three singleton-list checks. All counts are positive, so every saved list fails as a counterexample. No exhaustive coverage of any group is claimed.
claims.prior_art_relation: New experimental records only. They do not establish novelty of a mathematical theorem.

claims.exact_quantified_statement: For G equal to D_7 (n=14,q=7,s^2=1) or Dic_3 (n=12,q=6,s^2=r^3), for every k with 1<=k<=4, every a_0,...,a_k>=0, every b_0,...,b_(k-1)>=1, and every v_0,...,v_(k-1) in Z/qZ with sum(a)+sum(b)=2n-1, the word r^[a_0] (r^v_0*s)^[b_0] r^[a_1] ... (r^v_(k-1)*s)^[b_(k-1)] r^[a_k] contains an increasing-index n-term identity product. Bracketed exponents mean repetitions.
assumptions: G is one of the two fixed presentation groups.
All rotation letters are the single fixed generator r.
There are at most four constant reflection blocks.
claims.scope_detail: Restricted-family computational exclusion with analytic pruning. General words in either group and all other groups are outside this claim. This is not a Lean theorem or a full resolution.
claims.prior_art_relation: No originality claim for the restricted assertion. The known odd-dihedral one-short lower construction is not presented as a new finding.

coverage.primary_check: ordered product set DP plus proved pruning rules; not raw enumeration of every word

claims.exact_quantified_statement: For G equal to D_7 (n=14,q=7,s^2=1) or Dic_3 (n=12,q=6,s^2=r^3), every a_0,...,a_5>=0, b_0,...,b_4>=1 and v_0,...,v_4 in Z/qZ with sum(a)+sum(b)=2n-1 gives a word r^[a_0] (r^v_0*s)^[b_0] r^[a_1] ... (r^v_4*s)^[b_4] r^[a_5] having an increasing-index n-term identity product. Bracketed exponents mean repetitions.
assumptions: G is one of the two fixed presentation groups.
All rotation letters are the single fixed generator r.
There are exactly five constant reflection blocks.
claims.scope_detail: Restricted-family computational exclusion, using proved even-capacity and cyclic-cut/automorphism reductions. General words and the all-groups statement are not covered. No Lean proof or counterexample is claimed.
claims.prior_art_relation: An exact extension of this round's restricted-family experiment; no theorem-originality claim.
claims.coverage_note: Counts include duplicate words and analytically or symmetrically eliminated tuples. They use a leading rotation gap of zero after a cyclic cut and first reflection offset v_0=0. Other R values are excluded analytically.
